added_lemmas.statement:
There are numerical constants \(c,C<\infty\) and events \(\mathcal E_n\) such that
\[
 \inf_{P\in\bigcup_{\kappa\in K}\mathrm{Base}_\kappa}P(\mathcal E_n)
 \geq 1-Cn^{-3}.
\]
If \(n_1\geq1\), then, on \(\mathcal E_n\), simultaneously for every
\(h\in H_n\) and \(u\in U_n\) satisfying
\(n_1u\geq C\log(en)\),
\[
 J_P(h,u)
 \leq \widehat J\!\left(h,c\{u+\log(en)/n_1\}\right)
 \leq C\left\{1\vee
 J_P\!\left(h,C\{u+\log(en)/n_1\}\right)\right\}.                 \tag{P1}
\]
On the same event,
\[
 a^L(x,h)\leq a_P(x,h)\leq a^U(x,h)                              \tag{P2}
\]
for every \(x\in B\) and \(h\in H_n\), and
\[
 \tfrac12a_P(x,h)\leq a^L(x,h)leq a_P(x,h)leq a^U(x,h)leq2a_P(x,h) \tag{P3}
\]
whenever \(n_1a_P(x,h)\geq C\log(en)\).  For every \(h\in H_n\), the
source-labeled sorting, duplicate removal, deterministic refinement, and
midpoint operations defining \(C_1(h)\) and \(G_1(h)\) are Borel functions
of \((X_i)_{i\in I_1}\), and \(\widehat J(h,v)\) is Borel for every
\(v\geq0\).  In particular, the upper comparison in \((\mathrm{P1})\) uses
the same radius \(h\), and the floor \(1\vee J_P\) covers an empty population
thin set.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Put \(m=n_1\) and \(\ell=\log(en)\).  When \(m=0\), the condition
\(mu\geq C\ell\) has no solutions.  Moreover the definitions using
\(m\vee1\) give \(q_t^L=0\leq q_t\leq1=q_t^U\), hence \((\mathrm{P2})\).
It therefore suffices to consider \(m\geq1\).

For \(t\in\{0,1\}\), \(s\in[-1/2,1/2]\), and \(h\in H_n\), define
\[
 \mathcal C_{t,s,h}
 =\{z\in A_t:\|z-(0,s)\|_2\leq h\}.
\]
Fix deterministic points \(z_i=(r_i,s_i)\), \(1\leq i\leq N\).  If
\(z_i\in A_t\) and \(|r_i|\leq h\), then, as a function of \(s\),
membership of \(z_i\) in \(\mathcal C_{t,s,h}\) is the indicator of the
closed interval
\[
 \left[s_i-\sqrt{h^2-r_i^2},s_i+\sqrt{h^2-r_i^2}\right].           \tag{P4}
\]
Otherwise that membership indicator is identically zero.  Thus, for fixed
\((t,h)\), the trace on the \(N\) points changes only at the at most \(2N\)
endpoints in \((\mathrm{P4})\).  Since
\(|H_n|\leq2+\log_2 n\), the shatter coefficient of
\[
 \mathcal C_n
 =\{\mathcal C_{t,s,h}:t\in\{0,1\},\ s\in[-1/2,1/2],\ h\in H_n\}
\]
satisfies
\[
 \Pi_{\mathcal C_n}(N)
 \leq2|H_n|(2N+1)\leq C_0(N+1)\ell.                              \tag{P5}
\]

We next derive the relative empirical bound used below.  We first record a
finite-growth inequality.  Let \(\mathcal A\) be any class of measurable sets,
let \(P_m\) be the empirical measure of \(m\) independent observations, and
put
\[
 \Gamma=x+\log\{8\Pi_{\mathcal A}(2m)\},\qquad x\geq1.
\]
Then
\[
 \Pr\!\left\{\exists C\in\mathcal A:
 |P_m(C)-P(C)|>
 \sqrt{\frac{2P_m(C)\Gamma}{m}}+\frac{7\Gamma}{3m}\right\}
 \leq2e^{-x}.                                                       \tag{P6}
\]
Here is a proof.  Introduce an independent empirical measure \(P'_m\).
Conditional on the pooled \(2m\) observations, randomly pair the observations
and independently choose one member of every pair for \(P_m\), the other for
\(P'_m\).  This has the uniform random-split law.  For a fixed pooled trace,
the difference of its two counts is a sum of independent random signs, one
for every discordant pair.  If
\(\bar p=\{P_m(C)+P'_m(C)\}/2\), the number of discordant pairs is at most
\(2m\bar p\).  Therefore \(\cosh(v)\leq\exp(v^2/2)\) and exponential Markov
give
\[
 \Pr\!\left\{|P_m(C)-P'_m(C)|>
 2\sqrt{\bar p z/m}\,\middle|\,\text{pooled observations}\right\}
 \leq2e^{-z}.                                                       \tag{P7}
\]
Peel \(\bar p\) into the cells
\(2^{-j-1}<\bar p\leq2^{-j}\), together with \(\bar p=0\).  In each cell,
apply \((\mathrm{P7})\) with
\(z=\Gamma+(j+1)\log2\), and take a union over the at most
\(\Pi_{\mathcal A}(2m)\) pooled traces.  The sum over \(j\geq0\) is bounded
by \(e^{-x}/4\).  If \(d=|P_m(C)-P(C)|\), an independent application of the
same sign calculation to the ghost half shows that a violation of the bound
in \((\mathrm{P6})\) has conditional probability at least \(1/4\) of
producing a split for which
\[
 |P_m(C)-P'_m(C)|>
 \sqrt{4\bar p\Gamma/m}+2\Gamma/(3m).
\]
Indeed, substitute \(P(C)\leq P_m(C)+d\) when the deviation is downward and
\(P(C)\leq P_m(C)\) when it is upward, and use
\(2\sqrt{d\Gamma/m}\leq d/2+2\Gamma/m\); the constants
\(2\) and \(7/3\) leave the displayed margin after moving \(d/2\) to the
left.  Multiplication by four for this ghost step and the preceding geometric
sum prove \((\mathrm{P6})\).  This proof depends only on pooled traces, so it
also applies when the supremum is not attained, by taking an increasing union
over finite trace subfamilies.

Apply \((\mathrm{P6})\) to \(\mathcal A=\mathcal C_n\) with \(x=3\ell\).
The explicit first bound in \((\mathrm{P5})\) implies
\[
 \Gamma=3\ell+\log\{8\Pi_{\mathcal C_n}(2m)\}\leq6\ell
\]
for \(n\geq2\), by direct substitution of \(m\leq n/2\) and
\(|H_n|\leq2+\log_2n\); the case \(n=1\) has \(m=0\).  Consequently
\[
 \Pr\!\left\{\exists C\in\mathcal C_n:
 |P_m(C)-P(C)|>
 \sqrt{12P_m(C)\ell/m}+20\ell/m\right\}
 \leq C_1n^{-3}.                                                     \tag{P8}
\]
Closed intervals in \((\mathrm{P4})\) ensure that the pooled trace count
includes traces attained exactly at coincident or noncoincident breakpoints.

Let \(\mathcal E_n\) be the complement of the event in \((\mathrm{P8})\).
For \(x=(0,s)\),
\[
 P_m(\mathcal C_{t,s,h})=\widehat q_t^{(1)}(x,h).
\]
Therefore \((\mathrm{P8})\) and the definitions of \(b_n,q_t^L,q_t^U\)
give, simultaneously in \((x,t,h)\),
\[
 q_t^L(x,h)\leq q_t(x,h)\leq q_t^U(x,h).                          \tag{P9}
\]
Taking the minimum over \(t\) proves \((\mathrm{P2})\).  If
\(mq_t(x,h)\geq C_2\ell\), solving the two quadratic inequalities obtained
from \((\mathrm{P8})\) yields
\[
 \tfrac12q_t(x,h)\leq q_t^L(x,h)
 \leq q_t(x,h)\leq q_t^U(x,h)\leq2q_t(x,h).                       \tag{P10}
\]
When \(ma_P(x,h)\geq C_2\ell\), both side masses meet this premise.
Taking their minima in \((\mathrm{P10})\) proves \((\mathrm{P3})\).

We now construct the pattern-preserving representative.  Fix \(h\in H_n\).
Every endpoint in \((\mathrm{P4})\) generated by a first-half score and lying
in \([-1/2,1/2]\) occurs in the source-labeled candidate list.  Lexicographic
ordering is total; when labels have equal coordinates, retaining the least
label removes only duplicate labels and retains their common coordinate.
A deterministic mesh point tied with a breakpoint likewise occurs once in
the sorted union.  Define \(g_h((0,s))\) to equal \((0,s)\) when \(s\) is a
breakpoint, a deterministic mesh point, or an endpoint of \(B\).  Otherwise
there is a unique open cell \((w_j,w_{j+1})\) containing \(s\); define
\[
 g_h((0,s))=\left(0,\frac{w_j+w_{j+1}}2\right).
\]
No first-half membership indicator changes inside this open cell.  Because
\(M_h=\lceil16/h\rceil\), consecutive deterministic mesh points are at
distance at most \(h/16\).  Hence
\[
 \|g_h(x)-x\|_2\leq\frac1{2M_h}\leq\frac h{32}<\frac h4,
 \qquad
 \widehat q_t^{(1)}(g_h(x),h)=\widehat q_t^{(1)}(x,h)              \tag{P11}
\]
for \(t=0,1\).  At a breakpoint, equality follows from the closed-ball
convention and the choice \(g_h(x)=x\), so \((\mathrm{P11})\) also covers all
ties.

Let \(F\) be any \(h\)-separated subset of
\(\{x\in B:a_P(x,h)\leq u\}\).  For each \(x\in F\), choose a side
\(t_x\) with \(q_{t_x}(x,h)\leq u\).  On \(\mathcal E_n\), the inequality
\(|q_t-\widehat q_t^{(1)}|\leq b_n(\widehat q_t^{(1)})\) implies
\[
 \widehat q_{t_x}^{(1)}(x,h)\leq2u+64\ell/m.
\]
Indeed, putting \(z=\widehat q_{t_x}^{(1)}(x,h)\), one has
\(z\leq u+\sqrt{12z\ell/m}+20\ell/m\); solving this quadratic gives the
display.  Applying the definition of \(b_n\) once more and using
\(2\sqrt{uv}\leq u+v\), then using \((\mathrm{P11})\), gives
\[
 a^U(g_h(x),h)\leq C_3\{u+\ell/m\}.                               \tag{P12}
\]
For distinct \(x,x'\in F\), the triangle inequality and
\((\mathrm{P11})\) give
\[
 \|g_h(x)-g_h(x')\|_2
 \geq h-h/32-h/32=15h/16>h/2.                                    \tag{P13}
\]
The upward severity rounding in the estimator satisfies
\[
 u(v)\leq\min\{1,2v+m^{-1}\},\qquad v\geq0.                       \tag{P14}
\]
This follows directly from the adjacent ratio two of the positive dyadic
grid points; below its smallest positive point the excess is at most
\(m^{-1}\), and \(u(0)=0\).  Choose \(c\geq2C_3+1\).  Equations
\((\mathrm{P12})\)--\((\mathrm{P14})\) make \(g_h(F)\) feasible in the
maximum defining \(\widehat J(h,c\{u+\ell/m\})\), and
\((\mathrm{P13})\) makes \(g_h\) injective on \(F\).  Taking the maximum
over \(F\) proves the first inequality in \((\mathrm{P1})\).  The argument
remains well typed at \(u=1\), because the definition caps severity at one.

Conversely, let \(G\) be a nonempty feasible set in the finite maximum
defining \(\widehat J(h,v)\).  Equations \((\mathrm{P2})\) and
\((\mathrm{P14})\) imply, for every \(g\in G\),
\[
 a_P(g,h)\leq a^U(g,h)\leq u(v)
 \leq\min\{1,2v+m^{-1}\}.                                        \tag{P15}
\]
Order \(G=\{g_1<\cdots<g_M\}\) by boundary coordinate.  Feasibility gives
\(\|g_{j+1}-g_j\|_2\geq h/2\).  Because all points lie on the same line,
\[
 \|g_{j+2}-g_j\|_2
 =\|g_{j+2}-g_{j+1}\|_2+\|g_{j+1}-g_j\|_2\geq h.                 \tag{P16}
\]
Thus the odd and even sublists are each \(h\)-separated.  Equation
\((\mathrm{P15})\) already makes every one of their points thin at the same
radius \(h\).  The definition of \(J_P\) therefore yields
\[
 |G|\leq2J_P(h,2v+m^{-1}).                                        \tag{P17}
\]
If no nonempty feasible set exists, the maximum before flooring is zero and
the outer floor defining \(\widehat J\) equals one.  Combining the two cases,
substituting \(v=c\{u+\ell/m\}\), and enlarging \(C\) proves the second
inequality in \((\mathrm{P1})\).  Notice that no monotonicity in radius was
used: \((\mathrm{P15})\) precedes the odd--even split, so both population
packings in \((\mathrm{P17})\) are at radius \(h\).  The floor is necessary
precisely in the empty-thin-set case.

Finally, all the displayed sample maps are Borel.  The square-root endpoint
map is continuous on its closed domain.  Candidate inclusion and each
lexicographic comparison are Borel.  Sorting a list of bounded deterministic
length, retaining the least source label at a tied coordinate, adjoining the
deterministic mesh, and taking adjacent midpoints use finitely many Borel
comparisons and arithmetic operations.  The resulting \(G_1(h)\) is finite;
after encoding absent candidate slots by their Borel presence indicators,
the maximum defining \(\widehat J(h,v)\) is the maximum of finitely many
Borel feasibility indicators.  This proves the measurability assertion and
completes the proof.
added_lemmas.justification: This pure first-half lemma proves the sharper same-radius packing comparison, including the unit floor required when the population thin set is empty.
added_lemmas.gap: The former node mixed a valid empirical comparison with unproved second-half outcome-risk assertions and unnecessarily shrank the population radius.
added_lemmas.consumer: Any downstream oracle analysis may use the implementable count at its own physical radius, but must separately prove its selected-interval stochastic bound.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The replacement retains exactly the valid first-half comparison and measurability content, sharpens the upper comparison from radius h/8 to the same radius h, and removes the unproved outcome-risk and isolated-rate assertions. Inbound dependencies should migrate to the replacement and reopen for a separate stochastic proof.

proposed.comparator_claim: Theorem 1 gives a univariate pointwise minimax order under a regularly varying design density.
The paper studies pointwise smoothness adaptation for an inhomogeneous univariate design; its logarithmic lower bound concerns adaptation over smoothness, whereas L is fixed here.
The paper uses spatially normalized loss for univariate designs with finitely many density zeros.
The positive-density random-design supremum benchmark informs the regular endpoint only.
The submanifold-integral result assumes a design density bounded above and away from zero near the target submanifold.

The positive-density boundary class assumes a continuous density bounded away from zero, smoother conditional means, and finite moments of order 2+nu; only its conditionally sub-Gaussian overlap is comparable here.

The isotropic boundary result is stated on a continuous score-density class bounded above and away from zero near the boundary, so its upper theorem does not transfer to the larger vanishing-density class.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The empirical comparison is proved, but the general selected-bandwidth oracle and its regular-design corollary are not certified under the frozen class. The comparator table must therefore record context rather than matching by those reopened results.

open_obligations.what_is_open: A valid replacement for the selected-interval stochastic step leading to equation (23), uniformly over the frozen base class and without a global logarithmic factor.
open_obligations.obstruction: The proposed exposed-arc forest does not imply its block-mass bound. Consecutiveness says that each score enters and leaves a sweep at most once, but it bounds total variation by the mass of the union, not by the mass of one selected ball. Under the frozen assumptions that union mass can be arbitrarily larger than every member mass. Thus neither a population variance substitution nor a simultaneous Bernoulli count event can establish the asserted M6/M9 budget.
open_obligations.attempted: I repaired M9 by first seeking simultaneous upper and lower Bernoulli count bounds and then conditioning the sub-Gaussian sums on those counts. This controls each declared block, but the union bound still contains the number of sub-h exposed components because the claimed block-number bound is false. I also tried the unconditional binomial moment-generating function; it removes the invalid population-to-sample variance substitution but cannot remove the same missing entropy term.
open_obligations.partial_result:
The pure first-half result is complete: equations \((\mathrm{P1})\)--\((\mathrm{P17})\)
give the same-radius comparison, the factor comparison for \(a^L,a_P,a^U\),
and Borel measurability.  What does not follow from the frozen class is the
claimed selected-interval stochastic inequality.  At a fixed small radius
\(h\), place \(M\) boundary centers inside an interval of length less than
\(h/2\), and on each treatment side put a small score component near the
point at normal distance \(h\) from its corresponding center.  The components
may be chosen disjoint, each of mass proportional to \(h^\kappa\), while a
diffuse radial-power component supplies the common lower mass.  Each radius-
\(h\) ball then contains its own component but none of the other components.
The \(h\)-packing number of these centers is one, whereas the conditional
Gaussian averages contain \(M\) independent coordinates and have expected
maximum of order
\[
 \sigma\sqrt{\frac{\log M}{nh^\kappa}}.
\]
The frozen base class imposes no upper-mass, doubling, or sub-\(h\) entropy
condition that rules out this configuration.  Accordingly, a block-mass
bound proportional to one parent mass cannot be derived merely from
consecutiveness of individual membership paths.

prose_updates.tldr: The first-half geometry admits a complete, tie-safe, same-radius result: the empirical packing count is sandwiched between the population packing profile at the same bandwidth, with the necessary \(1\vee J_P\) floor, and every map is Borel. The former second-half no-global-log claim is not certified by this comparison. The frozen class permits arbitrarily many sub-bandwidth exposed score components inside one packing cell, so a selected-interval maximal inequality needs an additional entropy-controlling law property or a different estimator. The normalized flat witnesses and banked endpoint lower bounds are unaffected.

project_justification.gap: Boundary regression with vanishing one-sided mass requires both a measurable estimate of macroscopic thin-site multiplicity and control of within-cell empirical-process complexity. The frozen packing profile controls the first quantity but, without an upper-mass or local-entropy condition, not the second.
project_justification.niche: The closed contribution of this solve unit is the exact same-radius, empty-profile-safe first-half comparison. It identifies precisely which geometric information the empirical count does and does not recover.
project_justification.fill: A source-labeled breakpoint arrangement and deterministic mesh produce a Borel representative preserving every first-half membership pattern within distance less than \(h/4\). Odd-even splitting then converts empirical \(h/2\)-separation into population \(h\)-separation without shrinking the radius. The outcome-risk claim is separated out because its proposed exposed-arc block-mass estimate does not follow from the declared law class.

sampling_model.overlap: There is no treatment overlap at a fixed score. Nevertheless, the lower side-mass condition gives positive probability in every one-sided ball around each \(x\in B\), so \(x\) lies in the support of each restricted score law. Sharp assignment and consistency identify the observed conditional regression on side \(t\) with \(m_{t,P}\) almost everywhere there. The declared Lipschitz representative is continuous; two continuous representatives agreeing almost everywhere on a support agree at every support point, since a nonzero difference would persist on a neighborhood of positive restricted mass. Hence its one-sided limit identifies \(\theta_{t,P}(x)\), and differencing identifies \(\tau_P(x)\). This identification is setup, not the headline contribution.

prose_updates.related_work: Gaiffas (2005) studies univariate regularly varying designs and pointwise minimax behavior. Gaiffas (2007) studies pointwise adaptation over smoothness in an inhomogeneous univariate design; its logarithmic lower bound concerns smoothness adaptation, whereas the present Lipschitz constant \(L\) is fixed. Gaiffas (2009) treats univariate designs with finitely many density zeros under spatially normalized loss. These classes are neither included in nor supersets of the present bivariate side-mass class, so their theorems do not transfer directly. Cattaneo, Titiunik, and Yu assume a continuous score density bounded away from zero, smoother conditional means, and finite \(2+\nu\) moments. Only the conditionally sub-Gaussian overlap of that positive-density class is comparable with the regular subcase here; their upper results do not transfer to the larger vanishing-density class. Conversely, estimator-restricted lower bounds remain estimator-restricted. The same-radius empirical-packing lemma is proved directly and is not attributed to any of these results.
prose_updates.interpretation: At a fixed bandwidth, the first half can learn how many macroscopically separated thin boundary sites exist. It cannot, under the frozen law class alone, certify how many nearly tangent score components occur inside one such site. The distinction is immaterial for the normalized flat witnesses but material for a uniform theorem over every law in the base class.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The same-radius packing lemma is uniform over the declared base laws and allows atoms and arbitrary Borel score distributions. That generality blocks the proposed selected-interval forest: individual membership paths may be consecutive while the union swept inside one \(h/2\)-cluster has mass arbitrarily larger than a member ball. A valid no-global-log oracle would need a derived replacement argument, a revised estimator that counts within-cell patterns, or an explicit law-side upper-mass/local-entropy condition. The regular-design same-estimator corollary is therefore not re-added in this round because its cited oracle premise has reopened.
prose_updates.honest_scope: This round closes the pure empirical-packing and measurability result, including breakpoint ties, the case \(u=1\), the same physical radius on both sides of the comparison, and the \(1\vee J_P\) floor. It deliberately removes confidence-tail, zero-count, fallback-risk, and isolated-rate assertions from that lemma. The causal trace remains identified from the observed law by side support and Lipschitz continuity. The population oracle theorem, endpoint upper-rate adaptation, and regular-design same-estimator rate require a separate valid selected-interval stochastic bound; they are not consequences of the proved packing comparison alone. The flat-law membership theorem and banked endpoint lower bounds are unchanged.

statement_notes.justification: This proof-critical component supplies a tie-safe measurable selector and the sharper floored population comparison at exactly the estimator's bandwidth.
statement_notes.gap: It intentionally contains no outcome-risk assertion; the frozen packing profile alone does not control sub-bandwidth exposed components inside one packing cell.
statement_notes.consumer: Downstream arguments may invoke the first-half confidence and packing inequalities directly, while treating the second-half maximal inequality as a separate obligation.
